title: The support of a finite type quasi-coherent module is closed, locally the zero locus of the annihilator
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], with support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x\in X:\mathcal F_x\neq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2), $\mathcal F_x$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$ (a finitely generated $A$-module), and identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the point $x\in U$ corresponding to the prime $\mathfrak p_x\subseteq A$. Then $\mathcal F_x\cong M_{\mathfrak p_x}$, and $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ if and only if $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)=\{a\in A: aM=0\}\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$; that is, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\cap U=V(\operatorname{Ann}_A(M))$. Consequently $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is a closed subset of $X$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (morphisms-lemma-support-finite-type) part (1), via Lemma 056I (morphisms-lemma-support-affine-open), Properties Lemma 01PB (properties-lemma-finite-type-module) and Algebra Lemma 00L2 (algebra-lemma-support-closed, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex) as in its proof

proof.text: *Step 1 (the affine chart).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$. Let $g=\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ be the canonical open immersion with image $U$, and for $x\in U$ let $\mathfrak p_x$ be the prime with $g(\mathfrak p_x)=x$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; $g$ induces the identity of $A$ on global sections ($\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Let $\mathcal G=\mathcal F|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ be the restriction along $g$, $\mathcal G(W)=\mathcal F(g(W))$ with the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]; it is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2), and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal G)=\mathcal F(U)=M$ as $A$-modules. Since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c). The counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde M\to\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056I (lemma-support-affine-open): M = Γ(U, F) on U = Spec(A); Properties, Lemma 01PB (literature/stacks-project/properties.tex) for M finite; Schemes, Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine, literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex) for F|_U = M~

proof.text: *Step 2 (the stalk of $\mathcal F$ at $x\in U$ is a stalk on the chart).* Let $x\in U$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_x$. The map $W\mapsto g(W)$ is an order isomorphism from the open neighbourhoods of $\mathfrak p$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ onto the open neighbourhoods of $x$ contained in $U$ ($g$ is a homeomorphism onto the open $U$), and these are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods of $x$ in $X$ (intersect with $U$). Since $\mathcal G(W)=\mathcal F(g(W))$ with the same restriction maps, the directed colimits defining the stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] agree: $s_{\mathfrak p}\mapsto s_x$ ($s\in\mathcal G(W)=\mathcal F(g(W))$) is a well-defined bijective additive map $\mathcal G_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal F_x$ (well defined and injective by the description of equality of germs, surjective because every germ at $x$ is represented over an open inside $U$). It is $A$-linear for the actions of $A=\mathcal O_X(U)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)$ through the germ maps, because the $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}(W)$-module structure on $\mathcal G(W)$ is the $\mathcal O_X(g(W))$-structure transported along $g^\sharp$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056I (lemma-support-affine-open), proof: 'F_x = M_p' (the identification of the stalk of F at x with the stalk of F|_U at the point of Spec(A), which the source leaves implicit)

proof.text: *Step 3 ($\mathcal F_x\cong M_{\mathfrak p_x}$).* The isomorphism $\varepsilon$ of Step 1 induces an $A$-linear bijection $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}:\widetilde M_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal G_{\mathfrak p}$, $s_{\mathfrak p}\mapsto\varepsilon(s)_{\mathfrak p}$, with inverse $(\varepsilon^{-1})_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] the germ map $\lambda_M:M\to\widetilde M_{\mathfrak p}$, $m\mapsto\tau(m)_{\mathfrak p}$, is a localization of $M$ at $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$, so $m/s\mapsto s^{-1}\lambda_M(m)$ is an $A$-linear bijection $M_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}M\to\widetilde M_{\mathfrak p}$. Composing with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak p}$ and the bijection of Step 2 gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $M_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong\mathcal F_x$ (compatible with $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathfrak p_x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p_x}$). In particular $\mathcal F_x\neq0$ if and only if $M_{\mathfrak p_x}\neq0$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056I (lemma-support-affine-open), proof: 'the equality F_x = M_p, see Schemes, Lemma 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves) (7)'

Morphisms, Lemma 056I (lemma-support-affine-open) and Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type) proof of (1), second argument, with Algebra, Lemma 00L2 (algebra-lemma-support-closed, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex)

proof.text: *Step 5 (closedness).* $V(\operatorname{Ann}_A(M))$ is closed in the Zariski topology of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $g$ is a homeomorphism onto the open $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], so $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\cap U$ is closed in $U$ for every affine open $U$. The affine opens cover $X$ [def-pc-scheme], and $X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_U\bigl(U\setminus(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\cap U)\bigr)$ is a union of opens of $U$, hence of $X$; so $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is closed in $X$.
